summary: Elevated 5xx rate in prod us-east after model rollout - upstream runtime crashes + gateway circuit-breaker trips
description:
Issue summary: At ~2026-03-10T12:05Z we began a canary/staged rollout of a model variant (redwood-compat-v1 -> gptx-3-large) for BrightHealth AI's dedicated pool in us-east. Within ~3 minutes we observed a sustained spike in 5xx responses from the API gateway and increased upstream serving-runtime failures. Impact: BrightHealth AI reports ~30% error rate on /v1/generate endpoints, failures for synchronous requests, and streaming disconnects for chat sessions. Severity is customer-impacting (production traffic).

Impact details:
- Error profile: 502 and 503 from gateway, 500 and OOM/crash traces from serving-runtime workers, intermittent 504s from the load-balancer.
- Time window: 2026-03-10T12:08Z -> ongoing (mitigations applied 12:25Z).
- Customer-visible: failed inference calls, delayed processing of user requests, some webhook retries failing.

Environment: Dedicated pool for BrightHealth AI, prod, region us-east. Autoscaler configured for GPU-backed nodes with burst capacity. Canary rollout used 10% traffic routing to new variant.

Steps to reproduce / observed sequence:
1) Triggered canary rollout at 12:05Z routing 10% of customer traffic to gptx-3-large.
2) At ~12:08Z api-gateway started returning elevated 502/503. Circuit-breaker metrics showed rapid open events.
3) Serving-runtime logs show repeated worker restarts and OOM-like traces aligned with the model variant requests.
4) Autoscaler attempted to spin up additional nodes but observed Pod crash loops and failed readiness probes leading to capacity flapping.
5) Gateway escalated throttling and fallback policies for some routes, increasing 429s briefly then reverting to 5xx.

Relevant logs and telemetry:
- Kibana link (serving-runtime): https://logs.redwood.internal/app/kibana#/discover?_a=(query:(match:(message:(query:'oom|segfault|worker restart|gptx-3-large'))))
- Grafana dashboard (api-gateway error rates): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/AGW/error-rates?var-region=us-east
- SLO alert: api-gateway-p50-latency spike 12:09Z (alert ID: AGW-4271).
- Sample runtime stderr: "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc' at inference_loop.cc:412" (attached in incident bundle).

Initial hypothesis: The new model variant has a higher peak memory working set under the request mix used by BrightHealth AI, causing GPU memory pressure and worker process crashes. This combined with aggressive autoscaler/backoff and circuit-breaker thresholds at the gateway produced cascading 5xx errors. Secondary hypothesis: a kernel/driver mismatch in the dedicated pool exacerbated memory fragmentation under the new quantization layout.

Immediate mitigations attempted:
- 12:18Z: Scaled the canary back to 0% for BrightHealth AI (rollback candidate prepared).
- 12:20Z: Increased serving-runtime replica restart backoff and disabled quick-retry loops to reduce thrash.
- 12:23Z: Temporarily raised gateway circuit-breaker thresholds for the customer route to allow in-flight traffic to drain.
- 12:25Z: Eng started a hotfix branch to limit model cache pre-allocation.

Current status and next steps:
- Eng (runtime) to reproduce crash locally with a BrightHealth-like request corpus (action: Marcus Green).
- SRE to validate node driver/kernel versions in the BrightHealth dedicated fleet and check for recent node reboots (action: Liu Chen).
- Support to coordinate with BrightHealth AI on observed request characteristics and to verify whether they can hold traffic for a planned rollback to previous model (action: Ava Patel).
- If reproducer confirms memory pressure, proceed with model config changes (reduce batch size, disable certain ops) and re-run canary with expanded telemetry.

Customer communication: Notified BrightHealth AI at 12:22Z that we saw elevated errors and are investigating; provided ETA for next update 12:45Z.

Attachments: incident bundle (runtime crash dumps), sampling of failing request IDs, flamegraphs for model step.
comments: 2026-03-10T12:12Z - Ava Patel (Support): Acknowledged customer report. Collected request IDs and asked for permission to reduce canary to 0% if needed.

2026-03-10T12:20Z - Marcus Green (Runtime Eng): Observed repeated std::bad_alloc traces in runtime logs tied to gptx-3-large. Hypothesis: memory spike under specific tokenization path. Will attempt local repro with customer corpus.

2026-03-10T12:24Z - Liu Chen (SRE): Autoscaler logs show rapid scale-up attempts followed by pod crash loops. Checking node kernel versions and recent maintenance events in us-east. No node reboots in last 24h, but one GPU driver update rolled out 3 days ago (PR #812).

2026-03-10T12:28Z - Ava Patel (Support): Informed customer BrightHealth AI that we are rolling canary back to 0% as a mitigation and asked them to pause non-critical workloads. Customer accepted and is standing by for post-rollback verification.

2026-03-10T12:40Z - Marcus Green (Runtime Eng): Pushed hotfix branch that reduces pre-allocation for KV cache and patches a bad allocation path. Preparing a canary redeploy behind feature flag for staging tests.
2026-03-11T09:15Z - BrightHealth AI (Customer): Reported intermittent success after rollback but asked for root cause analysis and an ETA for a stable re-roll to gptx-3-large.
resolution_summary: Mitigation: rolled canary back to 0% for BrightHealth AI and applied temporary runtime backoff changes. Hotfix branch created to reduce memory pre-allocation; full RCA pending reproduction and driver validation. Customer currently on previous model variant; monitoring to ensure error rate remains at baseline.
follow_up_actions: Eng to validate hotfix in staging and run extended memory soak tests
SRE to audit node driver/firmware across dedicated fleet and rollback driver update if correlation confirmed
Update model rollout runbook with memory-safety checks and pre-rollout CVs for large models
Postmortem and customer-facing RCA to be produced within 72 hours
